Everything seems romantic and wonderful from a distance.

But never fear, there is a way out, I mean in! err, whatever.

It feels stagnant here.

Because it fucking is, you are, you probably work and TV/voat, over and over, like most of us do most of the time. So do something.

A good start? Hit up any museums nearby, I found a WWII Naval vessel and an impressive amount of space machines within a 4 hour drive, I can handle doing that round trip on a single day. These are generally pretty cheap, and I love history, I got started when I was reading history on wikipedia and found "surviving examples" listed and saw one of the neato machines I was reading about existed near me.

Fire up google maps and look for some green, find a wilderness area near you, buy a cheap but quality backpack (Surplus packs (alice, ilbe, filbe) present good bang for the buck, but are heavy, budget civilian packs are good too, no less than 50 liters) a decent tent, sleeping pad and bag, (around $400 of durable and reusable equipment, kelty is a good starter brand) and go overnight backpacking on the weekend, once you have the durable gear it will only cost you the gas you burn to get there, and food. Will be far more memorable than another weekend sitting on the couch or in the bar.

For a longer road trip, Pick something you always wanted to see in the US, some distance away, pull up some maps and look at what you can see nearby. I saw 5 major sites, monuments, and parks solely because I wanted to go see a site that was in a movie I liked, made a big loop through several states on my way there.

Then there is the crown, international travel. Pick a place, buy a lonely planet guide book, build up a couple thousand dollars, 2-3k should do it, and just fucking go. Its harder to make the jump than it is to keep going with your current life, but its worth it. Europe is expensive, the second and third world is where the adventure is. Use that backpack, try to look low rent, like a student if you can, and most of the bad element will leave you alone. Students can go almost anywhere, they arent worth robbing, they have little to no money. The most accosted I got while traveling was a drunk Russian who wanted me to drink with him, he was very drunk and was removed from the place. Though there was that girl in the Korean subway that I think intended to rob me, she came up babbling away in a very happy manner trying to hug me. I warded her off, smiling, trying to find out if I knew her, then she dropped her hands and walked away. When locals invite you somewhere, SAY YES! The worst that could happen is you get robbed, but you could have an incredible night.

Summing up Aspects of travel suck, realize as well that so long as you make it back, even a bad trip is a great story. There are 3 types of fun. Type 1 is fun, right now, as it is happening. Type 2 is fun in retrospect, in the story you get to tell. Type 3 is a life changing experience, something that changes everything about you and how you view the world.

I had a type 3 on my first trip out of the country, it was post communist europe, dirty, cold af, and I fell in love with being in far away places. Its been too many years since I left the country, I have to fucking go this fall or I might just explode.
